tasks.short: Run new-hire orientation and arrange supervised training on the job.

steps.what: Check new starters, roles, locations and required learning.
Agree suitable workplace practice, supervisors and adjustments with the line manager.
Arrange orientation dates, workplace sessions and invitations.
Assemble the orientation pack and supervisor checklist.
Welcome starters, explain expectations, answer questions and introduce workplace trainers.
Record attendance, assign follow-up learning and chase workplace sign-offs.

tasks.design: Configure role-based assignments in the {LMS} using authorised starter data from the {HCM}, with scheduling through the {CALENDAR}. A template generator assembles approved material from the {DOCS}; the {LMS} records attendance and requests supervisor attestation before marking workplace competence complete.
tasks.previous_blocker: Starter changes, local supervisor arrangements and learning records sit in separate places. The coordination work is fragmented even where enrolment features already exist.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing assignment and reminder features can handle much of the administration. Small integrations and template generators are cheaper to build and maintain with coding assistance; no model loop is needed here.
tasks.still_hard: Shift coverage, suitable supervisors, accessibility and a welcoming experience need local judgement. GDPR applies to starter and adjustment data; national rules may require employee consultation.
tasks.human_edge: Notice confusion, build trust and adapt explanations so starters feel able to ask for help.

ambition.what: A repeatable orientation route for starters on evening shifts.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time arranging sessions and assembling packs, and more time visiting workplace trainers. They can propose shift-specific learning routes; line managers retain staffing decisions.

reach.task: Coordinate the handover from starter administration to workplace readiness.
reach.learn: Starter-data quality, adjustment confidentiality and local onboarding responsibilities.

evidence.claim: Role-based assignments, scheduling, templates and attestation workflows are feasible without autonomous agents.
Live orientation remains substantial; the proposed time shares, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates.

assumptions: The company uses an {HCM} and {LMS}; approved exports can substitute for unavailable connectors.
Role requirements and reusable orientation material already exist.
Competence completion requires supervisor attestation, not merely a calendar event or attendance.
Build ranges cover one initial population; consultation and access delays may extend elapsed time.
unknowns: Which assignment, scheduling and attestation features are licensed in the {LMS}?
How are starter changes and supervisor availability maintained?
Which national consultation requirements apply?
Who can access adjustment requirements, and at what level of detail?
research_questions: Can existing enrolment rules handle role, location and shift without custom code?
Which orientation content is best discussed live, and which can be supplied beforehand?
How will supervisor attestations distinguish attendance from demonstrated competence?
new_work: Resolve missing starter data, scheduling conflicts and unassigned supervisors.
Maintain role-to-learning mappings and approved pack versions.
Review overdue attestations and disputed completion records.
Check access permissions and failed synchronisations.
tasks.statement: Conduct orientation sessions and arrange on-the-job training for new hires.

tasks.short: Evaluate instructors and programme effectiveness, then agree improvements.

steps.what: Retrieve attendance, assessment results and feedback responses from the {LMS}.
Observe instruction, practice activities and learner participation.
Read learner comments and observation notes in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Learner comments and instruction observation notes.
loop.output: Source-linked themes, contrary examples and questions requiring follow-up.
loop.check: Review cited excerpts, preserve minority views and exclude inferred instructor ratings.
loop.stop: One pass and one repair per course batch; ambiguous or sensitive comments receive manual review.
loop.why_not_simpler: Comments contain mixed meanings and context that fixed keyword rules miss.

steps.what: Calculate completion, assessment change and response rates in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Discuss evidence with the instructor and determine a fair performance assessment.
Draft recommendations for content, delivery and instructor support in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Human instructor assessment, evidence summary and calculated programme outcomes.
loop.output: Recommendations linked to evidence, with uncertainty and proposed follow-up measures.
loop.check: Reject unsupported causal claims, invented costs and changes to the human instructor assessment.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; disputed interpretations return to the manager.
loop.why_not_simpler: Recommendations must connect varied evidence to contextual teaching changes.

steps.what: Agree improvement actions, owners and review dates with the instructor.

tasks.design: Feed configured exports from the {LMS} into deterministic outcome calculations on the {DATA_PLATFORM} and a restricted {BI} dashboard. Bounded loops summarise comments and draft recommendations in the {DOCS}; observation, instructor assessment and agreement on improvements remain human.
tasks.previous_blocker: Feedback, observations and learning outcomes were hard to compare. Collecting them did not resolve whether teaching caused the observed results.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable calculations and evidence-linked text summaries reduce preparation. Faster implementation makes a small evaluation dashboard affordable without requiring automated personnel scoring.
tasks.still_hard: Response bias, small samples and differences between learner groups complicate evaluation. Fair instructor assessment needs context and an opportunity to challenge evidence.
tasks.human_edge: The manager distinguishes poor instruction from unsuitable content, learner circumstances or weak measurement and gives constructive feedback.
tasks.altitude: The manager spends more time observing teaching and checking whether improvements worked. Faster evidence supports monthly course decisions; employment and supplier-contract decisions retain their existing approval routes.

reach.task: Assess whether learning access and outcomes differ unfairly between employee groups.
reach.learn: Learn safe cohort aggregation, reasonable adjustments and the limits of outcome comparisons.

evidence.claim: Fixed outcome calculations and bounded comment summaries can reduce evaluation preparation; savings and build ranges are estimates.
GDPR Article 22 is relevant where instructor assessments produce significant employment effects.
AI intended to monitor or evaluate worker performance may fall within the AI Act employment category.
AI Act Article 26 includes worker information obligations for workplace deployment of high-risk AI.

assumptions: Time shares and remaining-time percentages are planning estimates informed by the supplied priors.
The initial design calculates programme measures and summarises evidence without generating individual performance scores.
The {LMS} holds evaluation responses and supports exports.
Build ranges cover a small programme pilot with agreed measures and existing hosting.
GDPR applies; AI Act classification depends on intended use. National consultation rules require separate assessment.
unknowns: Are instructors employees, external providers or both?
What employment consequences can an instructor assessment have?
Which baseline measures and follow-up outcomes exist?
Are observations and learner comments collected under an established policy?
Which country, representatives and approval arrangements apply?
research_questions: Which evaluation design can distinguish learning effects from differences between cohorts?
Does the intended use constitute worker-performance evaluation under the EU AI Act?
Which national rules govern consultation and access to instructor assessments?
new_work: Review comment summaries and contested evidence.
Maintain calculation definitions and observation rubrics.
Investigate missing responses and misleading cohort comparisons.
Track improvement actions and measure their later effects.
Maintain restricted access and respond to correction requests.
tasks.statement: Evaluate instructor performance and the effectiveness of training programs, providing recommendations for improvement.

tasks.short: Develop assessments and procedures for evaluating learning and its application at work.

steps.what: Agree learning outcomes and intended uses of assessment results.
Collect existing assessments, completion records and learner feedback.
Choose assessment methods, scoring criteria and follow-up measures.
Write assessment items, scoring guidance and evaluation procedures.

loop.input: Approved assessment specification, course materials and procedure template.
loop.output: Draft evaluation procedure with assessment items and source references.
loop.check: Validate required sections and outcome coverage; a subject expert checks accuracy and scoring.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per procedure; unresolved items return to the training specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates handle structure, but writing relevant questions and scoring guidance requires language interpretation.

steps.what: Pilot the assessment and observe confusing questions or impractical scoring.
Calculate pilot results and compare outcomes across assessment items.
Approve the revised procedure and release its controlled version.

tasks.design: An integration gathers evidence from the {LMS} and {DOCS}; a template generator uses a bounded drafting loop to prepare assessment procedures. Deterministic calculations feed a {BI} view, while version approval in {WORKFLOW} controls release to the {LMS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence was scattered, and writing questions required course knowledge. Existing templates did little to connect outcomes, questions and pilot results.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding lowers the effort of building connectors, coverage checks and report generators. A bounded model loop can draft from approved source material.
tasks.still_hard: Assessment validity, accessible testing and evidence of workplace transfer remain difficult. Small cohorts limit useful statistical comparisons.
tasks.human_edge: The manager decides what competent performance means and whether an assessment measures it fairly.
tasks.altitude: The week shifts from assembling evidence and formatting procedures to observing pilots and improving assessment quality. Authority to change assessment standards still requires explicit delegation.

reach.task: Design assessment items and pilot learning materials.
reach.learn: Assessment validity, item analysis and accessible assessment design.

reach.task: Review assessment barriers and accommodation needs.
reach.learn: Fairness review and how to distinguish learning measures from employment decisions.

evidence.claim: Templates, outcome coverage checks and pilot calculations can use deterministic code; question drafting needs expert review.
The design retains human decisions where assessment results could have significant employment consequences.
Using AI assessments for worker performance or promotion requires separate high-risk classification analysis.

assumptions: The main use is learning evaluation, rather than automatic promotion or dismissal decisions.
The {LMS} exposes assessment records through an approved export or interface.
Time shares and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured savings.
The judgement-heavy prior is retained; evidence assembly and calculations are more rule-covered than procedure design.
GDPR applies; national rules may require employee or works-council consultation.
unknowns: Which assessment results influence pay, promotion, role allocation or employment status?
Who currently approves assessment standards and procedure releases?
Are outcome identifiers and assessment versions recorded consistently?
What employee consultation and data-access arrangements already exist?
research_questions: Which assessment validation methods suit the expected cohort sizes?
What national consultation requirements apply to the proposed assessment use?
Which configured features in the existing {LMS} can replace custom development?
new_work: Review generated questions, scoring guidance and source references.
Investigate misleading pilot results and accessibility problems.
Maintain outcome mappings, templates and integration permissions.
Check retention and access controls for assessment data.

tasks.short: Arrange and deliver continuing technical training and personal development classes.

steps.what: Review training requests, required certifications and employee availability.
Agree course priorities, target groups and delivery format with line managers.
Book approved external provision and authorize the purchase commitment.
Prepare exercises, examples and session guidance for the selected cohort.

loop.input: Approved course materials, learning outcomes and cohort requirements without unnecessary personal data.
loop.output: Draft session pack with exercises and facilitator guidance.
loop.check: Check source references and required sections; the trainer verifies accuracy, accessibility and suitability.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per session pack; unsupported technical content returns to the trainer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates can assemble materials, but adapting examples and exercises requires language generation.

steps.what: Schedule sessions, rooms and trainer availability.
Enrol employees and issue joining instructions.
Deliver instruction, facilitate practice and respond to learners.
Record verified attendance and assessment outcomes, then request feedback.

tasks.design: Connect approved training needs from the {HCM} and {LMS}, then configure scheduling, enrolment and verified completion updates in the {LMS} and {CALENDAR}. A bounded generator prepares session packs in {DOCS}; purchase approval stays in {PROCUREMENT}, and trainers deliver the sessions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Roster changes, bookings and attendance crossed several systems. Cohort-specific preparation and delivery still needed a trainer.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing enrolment and notification features can handle much of the administration. Faster connector development and bounded drafting reduce the remaining preparation effort.
tasks.still_hard: Shift coverage, cancellations, accessibility needs and practical skills teaching remain costly. Attendance alone does not demonstrate competence.
tasks.human_edge: Trainers notice confusion, adapt practice and create the trust needed for honest questions.

ambition.what: Recurring technical training cohorts for shift workers

tasks.altitude: The manager spends more time observing teaching and arranging access for underserved groups. Budget and staffing decision rights do not expand automatically.

reach.task: Connect development requests with employee lifecycle events.
reach.learn: Role-based eligibility rules, minimal data sharing and roster quality.

reach.task: Adapt learning exercises and support facilitators.
reach.learn: Adult learning, accessible materials and facilitation for mixed experience levels.

evidence.claim: Scheduling, enrolment, reminders and verified completion updates are suitable for configured workflows.
The digest reports 2.8% hours saved across 11 occupations including HR; this does not establish training-manager savings.

assumptions: The {LMS} supports scheduled sessions, enrolment rules and completion imports.
A approved course plan identifies the audience before automatic enrolment.
Trainers supply verified assessment outcomes; the workflow does not infer competence from attendance.
Live delivery remains a large time share, consistent with the supplied relationship and meeting priors.
Time shares and build ranges are planning estimates.
GDPR applies; national rules may require consultation for changes to employee-data processing or monitoring.
unknowns: Which scheduling and notification features are already licensed and configured?
How are shift availability and release from operational duties recorded?
Which courses require observed practice or external certification?
Who can approve provider bookings and cohort priorities?
Which access and consultation processes apply?
research_questions: Can native configuration cover scheduling without custom optimization?
Which delivery formats improve access for shift workers without reducing practice time?
What national rules apply to mandatory training time and employee consultation?
new_work: Review generated session packs and technical examples.
Handle cancellations, missing attendance and roster mismatches.
Maintain enrolment rules, course ownership and connector access.
Check that reminders and enrolment do not disclose unnecessary employee information.
tasks.statement: Conduct or arrange for ongoing technical training and personal development classes for staff members.

tasks.short: Consult managers and survey employees to identify training needs from planned operational changes.

steps.what: Read operational change plans and role requirements in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Operational change plans and role requirements.
loop.output: Source-linked changes, affected roles, dates and questions for management.
loop.check: Verify dates and role references; preserve uncertainty about unapproved plans.
loop.stop: One pass and one repair per plan; missing or conflicting details go to the manager.
loop.why_not_simpler: Narrative plans describe process changes inconsistently and rarely specify learning implications directly.

steps.what: Prepare and approve survey questions about expected tasks, confidence and support needs.

loop.input: Consultation brief and an approved survey template.
loop.output: Short, neutral survey questions tied to the planned changes.
loop.check: The manager checks relevance, leading wording and unnecessary personal-data collection before approval.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; sensitive or disputed questions are written manually.
loop.why_not_simpler: A fixed template provides the structure, but questions need contextual wording for each change.

steps.what: Launch the survey, monitor responses and send reminders through the {WORKFLOW}.
Confer with operational managers about changing work, constraints and capability expectations.
Combine survey findings and management needs notes in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Survey responses, management needs notes and the consultation brief.
loop.output: A training needs draft distinguishing agreement, conflicting views and unanswered questions.
loop.check: Trace each proposed need to evidence; calculate response counts deterministically and flag underrepresented groups.
loop.stop: One synthesis and one repair; unresolved disagreements remain questions for validation.
loop.why_not_simpler: Reconciling narrative accounts requires interpretation; fixed counts cannot resolve differing meanings.

steps.what: Validate expected work changes, affected roles and unresolved needs with the training manager.

tasks.design: Configure approved surveys and reminders in the {WORKFLOW}, and keep change plans and consultation records in the {DOCS}. Bounded loops prepare briefs, survey wording and evidence-linked needs drafts; managers discuss the changes and validate the resulting needs before programme analysis.
tasks.previous_blocker: Operational plans were incomplete and managers expressed needs differently. Survey administration was easier to standardise than the conversations needed to clarify changing work.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing forms and reminders handle collection. Bounded reading and drafting make consultation preparation and synthesis cheaper while retaining human discussion.
tasks.still_hard: Managers may disagree about future work or describe preferences as capability gaps. Survey participation, confidentiality and uncertainty in change plans require attention.
tasks.human_edge: The manager asks follow-up questions, surfaces disagreement and builds enough trust for employees and managers to describe actual difficulties.

ambition.what: Pre-launch learning-readiness review for operational changes

tasks.altitude: More of the week goes to clarifying future work and testing assumptions with managers. Earlier readiness reviews can influence change plans, but they confer no automatic veto or budget authority.

reach.task: Include learning readiness in workforce planning for an operational change.
reach.learn: Learn change milestones, role-impact assessment and how to distinguish learning support from staffing changes.

reach.task: Plan employee consultation when changes affect work practices or employee-data collection.
reach.learn: Learn representative involvement, confidentiality expectations and applicable national consultation procedures.

evidence.claim: Configured surveys and reminders can automate collection while consultation and validation remain human.
Bounded text extraction and synthesis can prepare consultation evidence; the proposed savings are estimates.
The cited Dutch works-council law includes consent provisions for employee-data and monitoring arrangements; national rules elsewhere vary.

assumptions: Time shares and remaining-time percentages are planning estimates informed by the supplied priors.
The company already has a form capability in the {WORKFLOW}; otherwise a small deterministic form is required.
The pilot concerns one planned operational change and uses manually selected source documents.
No meetings are recorded automatically; reviewed notes provide the input.
Surveys identify group needs rather than rank individual employees.
GDPR applies. National rules determine whether employee or works-council consultation is required.
unknowns: Which operational changes and affected roles are sufficiently defined?
Can employees respond confidentially, and who may read raw responses?
Which employee groups need alternative ways to participate?
Which form capabilities and source-document access already exist?
Which country and employee-representation arrangements apply?
Who validates operational assumptions and owns unresolved questions?
research_questions: Which survey design reduces leading questions and nonresponse bias for this audience?
Which national consultation requirements apply to the planned work and data changes?
new_work: Approve contextual survey wording and maintain templates.
Review extracted changes and conflicting dates.
Check participation gaps and arrange alternative consultation.
Review synthesis for omitted concerns and unsupported conclusions.
Maintain access, retention and confidentiality settings.
tasks.statement: Confer with management and conduct surveys to identify training needs based on projected production processes, changes, and other factors.

tasks.short: Create and maintain training manuals, visual aids and learning materials.

steps.what: Find current policies, procedures, examples and existing learning assets.
Agree audience, learning objectives and technical scope with the subject expert.
Write explanations, worked examples, exercises and visual storyboards.

loop.input: Versioned source pack, audience description, learning objectives and content brief.
loop.output: Source-linked explanations, exercises and storyboards with unsupported points flagged.
loop.check: Require source references for factual claims, check objective coverage and have a specialist review teaching clarity.
loop.stop: One draft and two revisions per module; unresolved claims become questions for the subject expert.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates cannot turn varied procedures into clear explanations, realistic examples and coherent learning sequences.

steps.what: Format manuals, slides, diagrams and multimedia assets into reusable layouts.
Check technical accuracy and trial the material with representative learners.
Apply corrections, obtain release approval and publish the controlled version.

tasks.design: A generator collects versioned sources from the {DOCS}, uses a bounded loop to draft learning content, and renders manuals, slides and simple visuals through fixed templates. Validation records and release approval control publication to the {LMS}; source-version changes create review tasks in the {WORKFLOW}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Writing explanations and examples takes time, and each format requires repeated layout work. Source changes are hard to trace through copied material.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded drafting can work from a defined source pack, while deterministic rendering handles repeated layouts and version checks. Coding assistance lowers the cost of connecting these existing techniques.
tasks.still_hard: Technical correctness, instructional quality, accessibility and realistic demonstrations still need expertise. Bespoke animation, filming and complex media remain expensive; GDPR applies if examples contain personal data.
tasks.human_edge: Choose what learners must understand, spot dangerous omissions and test whether the material changes practical performance.

ambition.what: Plain-language companion modules for employees learning in a second language.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends more time setting learning objectives and testing material with learners, with less time rewriting and formatting. They can approve variants within validated technical scope and an agreed release policy.

reach.task: Design objective-linked exercises and check learning transfer.
reach.learn: Instructional design, accessible media and practical evaluation methods.

evidence.claim: Source-grounded drafting, template rendering and controlled publishing are feasible building blocks; the digest supplies no direct training-content case.
Technical review and learner trials remain necessary to establish material quality.
Time shares, remaining effort and build ranges assume reusable formats and are planning estimates.

assumptions: The first release covers a limited family of manuals, slides and simple visuals.
Sources have identifiable owners and approved versions.
Media rendering uses approved assets and templates; bespoke production is outside the estimate.
The loop drafts material but cannot publish it.
Access and consultation effort depends on source sensitivity and applicable national rules.
unknowns: Which sources are authoritative, current and licensed for reuse?
Which output formats and accessibility standards are required?
Who can validate technical content and approve release?
How much material requires filming, specialist illustration or translation?
research_questions: Which existing layouts cover enough material to justify a deterministic renderer?
Can source references survive export into every required format?
How reliably do source changes identify affected modules?
Do companion modules improve comprehension in representative learner trials?
new_work: Review generated claims, examples and exercise answers against sources.
Maintain templates, source mappings and rendering checks.
Check reading order, captions, contrast and exported layouts.
Review source-change alerts and withdraw obsolete versions.
Collect learner feedback and correct confusing material.
tasks.statement: Develop and organize training manuals, multimedia visual aids, and other educational materials.

tasks.short: Design, organise and deliver training that develops staff capability.

steps.what: Choose learning objectives, delivery methods and evaluation measures in the {DOCS}.
Develop explanations, demonstrations, exercises and facilitator guidance in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Approved source material, delivery plan and learning templates.
loop.output: A learning package with source-linked explanations, exercises and facilitator guidance.
loop.check: Check every objective is covered; review factual support, accessibility and exercise answers.
loop.stop: One draft and two revisions per module; unsupported technical content goes to the expert.
loop.why_not_simpler: Useful explanations and realistic exercises require contextual writing beyond template population.

steps.what: Check technical accuracy and safe practice in the learning package.
Approve the learning package for delivery.
Publish approved sessions and enrol eligible learners in the {LMS}.
Facilitate demonstrations, practice, discussion and feedback.
Record attendance and verified learning results in the {LMS}.
Discuss workplace application and barriers with learners and their managers.

tasks.design: Use approved sources and templates in the {DOCS} for bounded drafting of learning packages, with technical and delivery approval before publication. Configure the {LMS} to publish approved sessions, manage enrolment and record verified results; instructors deliver practice and managers discuss workplace application.
tasks.previous_blocker: Materials required repeated writing and revision. Existing course administration could automate logistics but could not judge technical accuracy or adapt instruction to learners.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded drafting can accelerate material development, while existing enrolment and completion functions can be configured. Faster code development helps connect approved packages to course administration.
tasks.still_hard: Specialist content, accessible exercises and effective practice require careful design. Attendance does not establish competence, and workplace application depends on supervisors and available practice.
tasks.human_edge: An instructor notices confusion, adjusts the explanation and creates a setting where learners can practise and ask difficult questions.
tasks.altitude: Less time goes to first drafts and course administration, leaving more time for practice and follow-up. A transfer clinic adds a service; authority over programme methods remains within the existing delegation.

reach.task: Design and run a supervisor-supported follow-up session after training.
reach.learn: Learn practice design, facilitator coaching and how to observe workplace application without creating employee scores.

evidence.claim: Course publication, enrolment and learning-record administration are commonly configurable functions of an {LMS}.
Source-grounded drafting can prepare learning materials, but experts still need to verify technical content.
The digest provides no documented training-delivery case validating the proposed time savings or build ranges.

assumptions: Time shares and remaining-time percentages are planning estimates informed by the supplied priors.
The manager coordinates delivery and may also teach; step shares include supporting roles.
The pilot covers one programme with available source material and established expert reviewers.
The {LMS} supports session administration, rule-based enrolment and structured result capture.
Only approved eligibility rules drive enrolment; no model assigns employees to opportunities.
GDPR applies to learner records. National consultation requirements depend on changes to learning and employee-data practices.
unknowns: Which course formats and enrolment functions are already supported?
Who owns source material and can approve its reuse?
Which subjects require accredited instructors or formal competency assessment?
What accessibility and language needs must the programme meet?
Can supervisors provide workplace practice and attend follow-up sessions?
Which country and consultation arrangements apply?
research_questions: Which accessibility and assessment standards apply to the proposed learning materials?
What follow-up design best supports workplace application for the chosen programme?
new_work: Review draft content, exercises and source references.
Maintain approved sources and regenerate affected modules when they change.
Handle enrolment exceptions and incorrect session results.
Check that recorded completion matches the required evidence.
Coordinate and evaluate the learning transfer clinic.
tasks.statement: Plan, develop, and provide training and staff development programs, using knowledge of the effectiveness of methods such as classroom training, demonstrations, on-the-job training, meetings, conferences, and workshops.

tasks.short: Analyse capability gaps and recommend new or improved training programmes.

steps.what: Retrieve course participation, assessment results and completion records from the {LMS}.
Read survey responses, validated training needs and role requirements in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Survey responses, validated training needs and role requirements.
loop.output: Evidence-linked themes, reported gaps and conflicting accounts.
loop.check: Require source references; check missing responses and review conflicts without inferring individual capability.
loop.stop: One pass and one repair per document batch; unsupported claims return to manual reading.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text descriptions express similar needs differently and often contain qualifications.

steps.what: Compare learning results and reported gaps by cohort in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Discuss whether gaps arise from skills, workload, tools or unclear expectations.
Develop programme options, objectives and evaluation measures in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Gap diagnosis, existing courses, evaluation findings and budget constraints.
loop.output: Comparable programme options with objectives, delivery choices and evaluation measures.
loop.check: Check costs against supplied rates, trace objectives to gaps and review practical suitability.
loop.stop: At most three options and one revision; missing costs remain explicitly unknown.
loop.why_not_simpler: Connecting contextual needs to learning activities requires bounded drafting beyond a fixed template.

steps.what: Select priorities and approve a programme brief within delegated authority.

tasks.design: Configure an export from the {LMS}, combine it with approved needs evidence on the {DATA_PLATFORM}, and publish cohort comparisons in the {BI}. Bounded loops prepare evidence summaries and programme options in the {DOCS}; the manager diagnoses causes and approves the programme brief.
tasks.previous_blocker: Learning records and qualitative needs were separate. Analysis also depended on local knowledge that reporting alone could not supply.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing exports, reusable data mappings and faster code development make the reporting practical. Bounded text extraction can reduce reading without claiming to diagnose capability automatically.
tasks.still_hard: Distinguishing a training need from an operational problem remains difficult. Small cohorts, inconsistent assessments and confidential comments limit useful comparisons.
tasks.human_edge: The manager challenges requests for training when better tools, clearer expectations or workload changes would help more.
tasks.altitude: The week shifts from assembling evidence to testing diagnoses and comparing interventions. Monthly prioritisation becomes feasible; formal budget and programme approval rights change only through explicit delegation.

reach.task: Identify role-specific onboarding gaps before new starters enter training.
reach.learn: Learn onboarding triggers, role requirements and the distinction between mandatory and optional learning.

evidence.claim: Structured learning exports and fixed cohort calculations can support needs analysis; proposed savings are estimates.
A study covering HR and other occupations found modest average chatbot time savings; it does not validate these task estimates.
GDPR Article 22 constrains solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects on employees.

assumptions: Time shares and remaining-time percentages are planning estimates informed by the supplied priors.
The initial scope uses cohort evidence rather than automated individual capability ratings.
The {LMS} supports scheduled exports; unavailable exports would require deterministic integration.
Build ranges cover one pilot business unit, existing hosting and a limited course catalogue.
GDPR applies to employee data. National rules may require consultation about new employee-data uses.
unknowns: Which learning records, assessments and role requirements are available and reliable?
What cohort sizes and access restrictions apply?
Who can approve programme changes and budget commitments?
Which country and employee-representation arrangements apply?
research_questions: Which cohort suppression and aggregation practices fit the intended analysis?
Which national consultation requirements cover the proposed employee-data use?
new_work: Review evidence summaries and unresolved conflicts.
Maintain cohort mappings, calculation definitions and source permissions.
Check whether recommended interventions address the diagnosed cause.
Monitor access logs and retention of qualitative comments.
tasks.statement: Analyze training needs to develop new training programs or modify and improve existing programs.

tasks.short: Evaluate training and apprenticeship programs against applicable government standards.

steps.what: Retrieve current official standards and record their versions.
Determine applicable requirements, exemptions and acceptable evidence.
Assemble curricula, instructor qualifications, attendance and assessment evidence.
Compare narrative evidence with requirements and document apparent gaps.

loop.input: Human-approved requirements matrix and versioned program evidence pack.
loop.output: Requirement-to-evidence table with citations, apparent gaps and explicit unknowns.
loop.check: Validate document references and requirement coverage; the reviewer checks each proposed conclusion.
loop.stop: One pass and one correction per program; missing or conflicting evidence is marked unresolved.
loop.why_not_simpler: Narrative curricula and instructor evidence rarely use the same wording as official requirements.

steps.what: Check required hours, dates, qualifications and record completeness.
Discuss gaps with program owners and agree corrective actions.
Sign the compliance review and record conditions for continued operation.

tasks.design: A versioned requirements register in {WORKFLOW} links official material from the {GOV_PORTAL} to evidence from the {LMS} and {DOCS}. Deterministic checks test structured requirements, a bounded loop drafts cited narrative comparisons, and the compliance manager approves the review before corrective actions are tracked in {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requirements and evidence used different formats, and applicable standards needed expert interpretation. Manual evidence gathering was repeated for each review.
tasks.enabler_now: Connectors, version checks and requirement tables can now be built with less development effort. Bounded document comparison can prepare traceable reviews without making the legal conclusion.
tasks.still_hard: Applicability, exemptions and whether evidence proves compliance remain expert decisions. Official source access and evidence quality can limit automation.
tasks.human_edge: The manager challenges weak evidence and decides when an apparent gap requires specialist advice or program changes.
tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time collecting records and more time resolving gaps before programs launch. Compliance sign-off and authority to suspend programs remain with designated decision makers.

reach.task: Maintain apprenticeship agreements and employee eligibility records.
reach.learn: Evidence requirements, document versioning and apprenticeship eligibility.

reach.task: Advise on employee consultation when training arrangements change.
reach.learn: Applicable national rules and the distinction between program review and employee monitoring.

evidence.claim: Versioned evidence registers and checks of explicit hours, dates and qualifications are deterministic design patterns.
Narrative evidence matching can prepare a review, but cannot establish legal applicability or certify compliance.

assumptions: Official standards are available from approved sources with stable retrieval methods.
A compliance specialist approves the requirements matrix before automated checks run.
The task ends with an internal review; government filing is a separate workflow.
The document-heavy prior is retained, with more time assigned to documented applicability than to meetings.
Time shares and build ranges are planning estimates.
GDPR applies to learner records; apprenticeship and consultation requirements depend on national rules.
unknowns: Which countries, qualifications and apprenticeship schemes are covered?
Are current standards and evidence available electronically?
Who has authority to sign reviews or restrict program operation?
What evidence retention periods and access permissions are approved?
Which employee or works-council consultation arrangements apply?
research_questions: Which official sources offer dependable change notices or versioned downloads?
What national requirements define acceptable apprenticeship evidence?
Which requirements can be expressed as explicit checks without legal interpretation?
new_work: Maintain approved requirements and source versions.
Review cited narrative comparisons and unresolved evidence.
Investigate failed checks and incomplete records.
Test rules after standards change and track corrective actions.
tasks.statement: Review and evaluate training and apprenticeship programs for compliance with government standards.

tasks.short: Coach instructors and supervisors in teaching skills and handling employee situations.

steps.what: Review learner feedback and previous trainer observations.

loop.input: De-identified learner feedback and trainer observations from a defined period.
loop.output: Development themes with source references, conflicting evidence and unanswered questions.
loop.check: Require a source reference for each theme; the manager checks interpretation and removes unsupported claims.
loop.stop: One classification pass and one correction pass; unclear material goes to the manager.
loop.why_not_simpler: Feedback uses varied language and context; fixed tags alone miss explanations and conflicting observations.

steps.what: Agree the coaching goals and employee situations to practise.
Prepare exercises, facilitator notes and observation checklists.

loop.input: Learning objectives, approved teaching guidance and fictional employee situations.
loop.output: Exercises and facilitator notes rendered into standard templates.
loop.check: Check policy references, objective coverage, accessibility and respectful treatment; the manager reviews suitability.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per pack; unresolved policy questions go to a human resources specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates handle layout, but tailored practice dialogue and feedback prompts require contextual writing.

steps.what: Demonstrate teaching techniques and facilitate practice with feedback.
Observe a teaching session and agree individual coaching actions.
Record agreed development actions and schedule follow-up.

tasks.design: Use bounded loops to summarise de-identified feedback and draft exercises from approved material in the {DOCS}. Configure the {LMS} and {CALENDAR} to record agreed actions and arrange follow-up; the manager conducts practice, observes teaching and gives personal feedback.
tasks.previous_blocker: Session preparation is bespoke, while feedback arrives as free text. Coaching itself depends on trust, observation and sensitive interpretation.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded drafting can produce useful first versions from approved sources. Existing learning records and reminders can carry agreed actions without generating employee scores.
tasks.still_hard: Fair coaching requires context and psychological safety. GDPR applies to feedback; using AI to evaluate workers or affect career opportunities needs a separate EU AI Act assessment and consideration of national rules.
tasks.human_edge: Read the room, challenge unhelpful behaviour and give feedback that a supervisor can accept and use.

ambition.what: A first-session coaching clinic for newly appointed workplace trainers.

tasks.altitude: Preparation takes less of the week, leaving more time for observed practice and follow-up. The manager can tailor coaching within the agreed programme; performance and employment decisions remain with authorised managers.

reach.task: Help supervisors recognise when an employee conversation needs formal escalation.
reach.learn: Employee representation, national rules and the boundary between coaching and formal case handling.

evidence.claim: Bounded feedback classification and exercise drafting can assist preparation; their usefulness needs local validation.
The EU AI Act identifies specified employment evaluation and monitoring uses as high-risk.
Applicable high-risk workplace deployments include duties to inform workers and their representatives before use.
Time shares, remaining effort and build ranges are estimates, not documented results for trainer coaching.

assumptions: The initial scope supports development and does not produce automated worker ratings.
Practice situations are fictional or sufficiently de-identified.
Approved employee policies and teaching guidance are available.
Consultation ranges describe working effort; formal procedures may take longer in elapsed time.
unknowns: Does trainer feedback also feed formal performance or promotion decisions?
Can feedback be de-identified without losing necessary context?
Which national consultation and employee-representation requirements apply?
Who approves sensitive employee-relations content?
research_questions: Can existing feedback categories handle enough material to avoid a classification loop?
Do generated exercises improve preparation time without weakening practice quality?
What source detail does a manager need to challenge a proposed development theme?
new_work: Review feedback themes for omitted context and unfair generalisations.
Check exercises against current policy and remove identifying details.
Maintain prompt examples, templates and source permissions.
Handle feedback disputes and route formal employee issues to the appropriate specialist.
tasks.statement: Train instructors and supervisors in techniques and skills for training and dealing with employees.

tasks.short: Align internal courses with regional education providers and define training pathways and procedures.

steps.what: Collect provider course outlines, prerequisites, dates and qualification details.

loop.input: Provider course outlines and timetables received through approved channels.
loop.output: Course records with prerequisites, dates, qualifications and source references.
loop.check: Validate fields and dates; the coordinator checks ambiguous prerequisites and credential claims.
loop.stop: One extraction and one retry per document; ambiguous fields remain blank for manual confirmation.
loop.why_not_simpler: Providers supply differently worded documents; structured imports should replace the loop where available.

steps.what: Compare provider courses with internal outcomes, prerequisites and timetable constraints.
Discuss course fit, recognition, learner support and delivery arrangements with providers.
Draft sequencing, attendance, assessment and support procedures.

loop.input: Proposed pathway, confirmed provider terms and approved internal procedure template.
loop.output: Draft training procedure showing sequence, responsibilities and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Validate required sections; the specialist verifies that recognition and support terms match confirmed agreements.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per pathway; unresolved commitments return to the training manager.
loop.why_not_simpler: A template cannot fully express negotiated responsibilities and differences between internal and provider practices.

steps.what: Approve the pathway and designate its training procedures.
Confirm places and purchasing commitments with the provider.
Publish the agreed pathway and enrolment instructions to employees.
Record approved course mappings, prerequisites and procedure links.

tasks.design: A course register in the {LMS} stores provider offerings and approved mappings; deterministic comparisons show prerequisites and timetable conflicts. Bounded loops extract inconsistent provider documents and draft procedures in {DOCS}, while configured flows in {PROCUREMENT} and {WORKFLOW} manage approved bookings and publication.
tasks.previous_blocker: Provider information arrived in inconsistent documents, and course recognition depended on negotiation. Small volumes made bespoke integration difficult to justify.
tasks.enabler_now: A reusable register and document importer are cheaper to build with AI-assisted coding. Existing approval and notification features handle the administration after agreement.
tasks.still_hard: Credit recognition, provider capacity, learner support and release from work remain negotiated matters. Low annual volume may still make configuration the best investment.
tasks.human_edge: The manager builds provider relationships and judges whether a pathway will work for actual learners.

ambition.what: Vocational qualification pathways for employees without formal qualifications

tasks.altitude: The manager spends more time discussing pathway quality and learner support, with less document copying. Authority to commit spending or recognize qualifications still requires explicit delegation.

reach.task: Map internal learning outcomes to external course requirements.
reach.learn: Qualification frameworks, prerequisite mapping and recognition of prior learning.

reach.task: Assess how funded education fits development benefits.
reach.learn: Education funding rules, repayment terms and applicable national rules.

evidence.claim: Course registers, prerequisite comparisons and approved booking flows can use configuration and deterministic code.
Provider negotiations and qualification recognition remain human decisions; bounded loops can prepare their documents.

assumptions: Regional vocational or professional education providers are the typical European equivalent of community schools.
Providers offer documents or structured catalogues that may be reused with permission.
Comparisons use explicit prerequisites and approved outcome mappings, without automatic claims of qualification equivalence.
The human-class prior remains appropriate for relationship work; preparation and administration can still change.
Time shares and build ranges are planning estimates.
GDPR applies to learner information; national rules govern funding, employment terms and consultation.
unknowns: Which providers and qualification pathways are already used?
Are course equivalencies formally recognized or only internal recommendations?
Who approves spending, qualification recognition and learner support?
Which employees lack access to existing pathways?
What access permissions and consultation arrangements apply?
research_questions: Which regional qualification frameworks support recognition of prior learning?
Can provider catalogues be imported through structured interfaces?
What national funding and employment rules apply to the proposed pathways?
new_work: Check extracted provider terms and maintain catalogue versions.
Review drafted procedures and confirm unresolved provider commitments.
Maintain approved mappings and handle timetable exceptions.
Monitor whether new pathways deliver useful qualifications and adequate learner support.
tasks.statement: Coordinate established courses with technical and professional courses provided by community schools, and designate training procedures.

tasks.short: Prepare the training budget, compare options and secure financial approval.

steps.what: Extract training spend, commitments, participation and headcount.
Collect departmental learning requests, attendance estimates and supplier quotes.
Reconcile costs, commitments and demand to common categories and periods.
Calculate programme costs and compare delivery, participation and timing scenarios.
Agree learning priorities and trade-offs with department heads and finance.
Prepare the budget submission and obtain approval for the allocation.

tasks.design: Scheduled imports into the {DATA_PLATFORM} reconcile authorised exports from the {ERP}, {PROCUREMENT}, {LMS} and {HCM}, while forms in the {WORKFLOW} collect demand and cost assumptions. Deterministic calculations feed scenarios in the {BI} and a templated submission in the {DOCS}; approval in the {WORKFLOW} records the authorised budget without placing orders.
tasks.previous_blocker: Finance categories, learning records and departmental requests do not align. Manual consolidation hides the assumptions behind apparently precise totals.
tasks.enabler_now: A small data model, reconciliation rules and scenario calculator can connect structured inputs. Coding assistance reduces implementation effort; a model loop adds little to the core calculation.
tasks.still_hard: Demand, supplier prices and the value of training remain uncertain. Leaders must choose priorities; GDPR requires proportionate use of employee data, and national rules may affect consultation on training plans.
tasks.human_edge: Defend necessary learning, challenge weak demand estimates and negotiate trade-offs between departments.

ambition.what: A monthly decision on reallocating uncommitted training funds.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time assembling totals and more time discussing options with finance and department heads. They can propose monthly reallocations with current evidence; spending authority changes only if explicitly delegated.

reach.task: Compare training investment with other employee development benefits.
reach.learn: Total reward budgeting, eligibility design and consistent treatment of employee groups.

evidence.claim: Structured intake, reconciliation rules, scenario calculations and templated submissions can automate budget preparation without a model loop.
Budget preparation can be substantially assisted, while allocation priorities and financial approval remain human decisions.
Time shares, remaining effort and build ranges are estimates; the digest contains no directly comparable training-budget case.

assumptions: Initial integration can use approved periodic exports.
The budget model separates invoices, commitments and new demand to prevent double counting.
Departments enter quote totals into structured fields; extracting varied quote documents is outside the initial scope.
Cost assumptions explicitly cover relevant travel, trainer time, employee time and applicable taxes.
The finance director is the assumed final approver; the actual delegation schedule governs.
Consultation and access ranges cover working effort, with possible longer elapsed lead times.
unknowns: How are training costs and open commitments coded in the {ERP} and {PROCUREMENT}?
Which internal labour and opportunity costs belong in the budget?
Who holds approval and reallocation authority?
Can existing planning features cover the scenario model?
Which employee consultation requirements apply under national rules?
research_questions: Can existing finance planning configuration replace a custom calculator?
Which reconciliation checks catch the largest budget errors?
Which uncertain assumptions materially change programme choices?
Would monthly reallocation improve decisions enough to justify the review effort?
new_work: Maintain account mappings, cost assumptions and scenario rules.
Resolve missing commitments, duplicate requests and reconciliation exceptions.
Review data freshness and explain forecast changes.
Retain approval records and update authorised budget versions.
tasks.statement: Prepare training budget for department or organization.

More frequent programme decisions become feasible; formal spending, employment and change-approval rights require explicit delegation.

Work with labor relations specialists on consultation for changed work and employee-data practices.

Defining defensible learning and transfer measures

Labor relations specialist: recognise when coaching needs formal employee-relations support.
Training and development specialist: strengthen instructional design and evaluation.
Compensation and benefits manager: assess learning investment within the wider employee offer.
skills_to_grow: Configure learning assignments, attestations and reminders.
Define reusable data mappings, reconciliation checks and cost assumptions.
Evaluate source-grounded drafts and maintain controlled learning content.
Observe teaching and measure practical learning transfer.
Apply GDPR, assess relevant EU AI Act uses and work with national consultation requirements.
role_batches.ambitious_version: Run a learning service that reaches shift workers, supports new workplace trainers and offers plain-language material, supported by a monthly investment review. Begin with reusable templates and authorised exports, then add integrations where repeated use justifies their upkeep.

role_batches.altitude: The week shifts toward teaching quality, assessment validity, provider relationships and early resolution of compliance gaps. Administrative capacity increases; spending, employment and compliance decision rights require explicit delegation.
reach: Training and development specialist: assessment design and qualification mapping.

summary.basis: 100 baseline hours; equal weight per loaded task; step shares normalized within each task
